q: Under the National Building Code of the Philippines, a building permit shall expire and become null and void if the authorized work is not commenced within what period from the date of issuance?
n: A building permit becomes null and void if the work is not started within one year of issuance, or is suspended or abandoned for 120 days. Source: NBC (PD 1096), Sec. 305.

q: Public buildings and traditional indigenous family dwellings are exempt from the payment of building permit fees. To gain such exemption, traditional family dwellings should be intended for the use and occupancy by the family of the owner only and be made of native materials. Finally, the total cost of such dwelling should not exceed how much?
n: A traditional indigenous family dwelling is exempt from fees if built of native materials for the owner's family only and costing no more than ₱15,000. Source: NBC (PD 1096), Sec. 208.

q: Failure to post Building Permit construction information sign constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Failure to post the construction information sign is a Light Violation, fined ₱5,000. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.i(b).

q: Failure to post Certificate of Occupancy/Use/Operation constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Failure to post the Certificate of Occupancy/Use/Operation is a Light Violation (₱5,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.i(a).

q: Excavations left open without any work being done in the site for more than one hundred twenty (120) days constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Excavations left open with no work for more than 120 days are a Grave Violation (₱10,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.iii(f).

q: Failure to provide or install appropriate safety measures for the protection of workers, inspectors, visitors, immediate neighbors and pedestrians constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Failure to provide safety measures for workers, inspectors, visitors, neighbors and pedestrians is a Light Violation (₱5,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.i(c).

q: Non-compliance with work stoppage order for construction/demolition without permit constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Ignoring a work stoppage order for construction or demolition without a permit is a Grave Violation (₱10,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.iii(d).

q: Non-compliance with the work stoppage order for the alteration/addition/ conversion/repair without permit constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Ignoring a work stoppage order for alteration, addition, conversion or repair without a permit is a Less Grave Violation (₱8,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.ii(a).

q: Change in the existing use or occupancy without Certificate of Change of Occupancy/Use/Operation constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Changing the existing use or occupancy without a Certificate of Change of Occupancy is a Grave Violation (₱10,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.iii(e).

q: Use or occupancy of building/structure without appropriate Certificate of Occupancy/Use/Operation constitutes what kind of violation?
n: Using or occupying a building without the appropriate Certificate of Occupancy is a Less Grave Violation (₱8,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.ii(b).

q: Unauthorized change in type of construction from more fire-resistive to less fire-resistive constitutes what kind of violation?
n: An unauthorized change in construction type from more fire-resistive to less fire-resistive is a Grave Violation (₱10,000). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.iii(b).

q: A contractor begins foundation excavation and site preparation without first securing the required Building Permit. The Office of the Building Official subsequently issues a Notice of Violation and a Work Stoppage Order. Despite these actions, construction activities continue at the site. What is the MOST serious violation committed by the contractor?
o: Non-compliance with a Work Stoppage Order
Unauthorized excavation and site development works without the necessary permit
Failure to comply with permitting requirements prior to construction
n: Building without a permit is already a violation. Continuing after a Work Stoppage Order for construction without a permit is classed as a Grave Violation, the most serious here. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212.2.a.iii(d).

q: If you were to build a structure near a body of water in Manila, where will you ask for an additional permit?
n: Metro Manila lies within the Laguna de Bay region. Projects there, especially near water bodies, need LLDA clearance in addition to the building permit. Source: RA 4850 (LLDA Charter), as amended by PD 813 and EO 927.

q: Easement along bodies of water shall be how many meters from the sides of waterways in urban areas?
n: The Water Code sets a 3 m easement along the banks of waterways in urban areas, 20 m in agricultural areas and 40 m in forest areas. Source: PD 1067 (Water Code), Art. 51; NBC IRR, Table VIII.G.1.

q: Easement along bodies of water shall be how many meters from the sides of waterways in agricultural areas?
n: The easement along waterways in agricultural areas is 20 m. Source: PD 1067 (Water Code), Art. 51; NBC IRR, Table VIII.G.1.

q: Easement along bodies of water shall be how many meters from the sides of waterways in forest areas?
n: The easement along waterways in forest areas is 40 m. Source: PD 1067 (Water Code), Art. 51; NBC IRR, Table VIII.G.1.

q: Which government agency is primarily responsible for the control of noise pollution coming from industrial establishments?
n: The DENR, through its Environmental Management Bureau, regulates noise pollution from industrial establishments under the pollution-control laws. Source: PD 984 (Pollution Control Law) and DENR/EMB rules.

q: EO 26 series of 2017 mandates smoke-free environments in public and enclosed spaces. Designated smoking areas should be established how far away from entrances, exits and places where people congregate?
n: EO 26 (2017) requires designated smoking areas to be at least 10 m from entrances, exits and places where people pass or gather. Source: Executive Order No. 26, s. 2017, Sec. 4.

q: What is the minimum depth for a footing according to PD 1096?
n: Footings must be at least 600 mm below the ground surface. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII (Light and Ventilation for Dwellings), Sec. 808 / Rule on Foundations for R-1 dwellings.

q: What is the minimum thickness of footing as per PD 1096
n: Footings must be at least 250 mm thick. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule on Foundations for dwellings (Footing: 250 mm thick, 600 mm below grade).

q: Provided by the owner when applying for a Building Permit
n: The owner supplies proof of land ownership, the TCT (or a lease contract or deed of sale), with the building permit application. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.3 (documentary requirements).

q: The owner does not wish to be troubled by the Building Permit application and thus wants the architect to do it for him instead. What should he provide the architect?
n: An owner who wants the architect to file for him must give a notarized Special Power of Attorney, which authorizes the architect to act for him before the OBO. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.3; Civil Code, Art. 1878.

q: While processing a Building Permit application, the Office of the Building Official (OBO) requests additional documentary requirements that are not included in the official checklist or applicable regulations. What is the MOST appropriate action for the architect?
o: Refuse to provide the documents and immediately elevate the matter to the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC).
Request clarification and the legal basis for the additional requirements, while complying with any requirements that are supported by applicable laws, codes, or local ordinances.
Submit all requested documents immediately to avoid delays in permit processing.
Advise the owner to proceed with construction while waiting for the OBO to resolve the issue.
n: The architect should ask for clarification and the legal basis, and comply with whatever the law, code or ordinances actually require. The OBO may not impose requirements outside the official checklist. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302 (only prescribed documents are required); RA 11032 (Ease of Doing Business Act), Sec. 9.

q: A building permit will become null and void if work is not commenced within one (1) year from its issuance or if it was commenced but work was suspended or abandoned for a period of how many days?
n: A permit lapses if work does not start within one year of issuance, or if it is suspended or abandoned for 120 days after starting. Source: NBC (PD 1096), Sec. 305.

q: Who is primarily responsible for the preparation of shop drawings in a construction project governed by CIAP?
n: Shop drawings are prepared by the contractor (or subcontractor or supplier) to show how the work will be fabricated and installed. The architect reviews them. Source: CIAP Document 102, Uniform General Conditions of Contract for Private Construction (shop drawings).

q: Which type of drawing typically shows room dimensions, furniture placements, finishes, and their corresponding specifications and sources?
n: The architectural interior plan shows room dimensions, furniture layout and finishes, with their specifications and sources. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302 (architectural documents: architectural interior plans).

q: What do you call the post-construction drawings prepared by the contractor and verified by the Architect-in-Charge of Construction (AICC), which reflect the final built condition of a project including all modifications, deviations, and field adjustments from the original design?
n: As-built drawings are prepared after construction by the contractor and verified by the AICC. They record the final built condition, including all changes and field adjustments. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III (Certificate of Occupancy requirements: as-built plans).

q: Who can sign and seal Architectural Plans?
n: Only a Registered and Licensed Architect may sign and seal architectural plans and documents. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20 and Sec. 29.

q: Who can sign and seal electrical drawings?
n: Electrical plans for permit must be signed and sealed by a Professional Electrical Engineer. Source: RA 7920 (New Electrical Engineering Law), Sec. 2 and Sec. 21; NBC IRR, Rule III (electrical documents).

q: Size of a rectangular dining table for 8 people if its width is 1.00 m
n: Each diner needs about 0.60 m of table edge. Eight people seat four per side, so the table is 4 × 0.60 = 2.40 m long. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design and Space Planning, dining space (0.60 m per place setting).

q: Size of a square dining table for 2 people (inches)
n: A square table for two is typically 30 in × 30 in (about 0.76 m), the smallest size that gives each diner a full place setting. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design and Space Planning, table sizes.

q: A fire-resistant wall designed to prevent the spread of fire and smoke within a building. It is also used to compartmentalize spaces within a structure, thus slowing fire progression and giving occupants more time to evacuate and firefighters a better chance to control the blaze.
n: A fire barrier is a fire-resistance-rated wall inside a building that compartmentalizes spaces to slow fire and smoke spread. A fire wall separates buildings or fire areas and runs from foundation to roof. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Definition of Terms.

q: What is the minimum thickness required for a concrete wall partition to qualify as a two-hour fire-resistive occupancy separation?
n: Table VI.1 sets 150 mm of solid concrete for a 2-hour partition (125 mm for 1 hour, 175 mm for 3–4 hours). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Table VI.1.

q: What is the minimum required thickness of a concrete firewall to achieve a four-hour fire-resistive rating, as prescribed by Philippine building and fire safety standards?
n: Table VI.1 sets 175 mm of solid concrete for a 4-hour partition (180 mm for an exterior wall). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Table VI.1.

q: The portion of a roadway or public way that should be kept open and unobstructed at all times for the expedient conduct of firefighting operations
n: A fire lane is the part of a roadway or public way kept open and unobstructed at all times so firefighting operations can proceed quickly. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Definition of Terms.

q: As per NBCP, fire-resistive buildings are classified under what type? Its structural elements shall be of steel, iron, concrete or masonry construction. Walls, ceilings and permanent partitions shall be of incombustible fire-resistive construction.
n: Type V buildings are four-hour fire-resistive throughout. Their structural elements are steel, iron, concrete or masonry, and walls, ceilings and permanent partitions are incombustible fire-resistive construction. Source: NBC (PD 1096), Sec. 401; IRR Rule IV.

q: Why is concrete considered one of the most fire-resistant building materials?
o: It expands when exposed to high temperatures, thereby increasing its fire-resistance rating.
It reflects heat away from the structure and prevents flames from reaching structural members.
It contains moisture, has low thermal conductivity and is non-combustible, allowing it to resist the transfer of heat and maintain structural integrity during a fire.
It contains naturally occurring fire-retardant chemicals that extinguish flames upon contact.
n: Concrete is non-combustible, holds moisture and conducts heat slowly. It resists heat transfer and keeps its structural integrity in a fire. Source: NBC IRR, Table VI.1 (concrete thickness for fire resistance); fire-protection references on concrete.

q: Maximum door leaf width of an exit door
n: No leaf of an exit door may be wider than 1.20 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.3.d.

q: Doorknobs and other hardware should be located between what heights above the floor?
n: The original BP 344 IRR places doorknobs and other hardware 0.82 m to 1.06 m above the floor. The 2024 amendment centers them at 900 mm. Source: BP 344 IRR (1983), Doors; Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 2.11.

q: Vertical pull handles should be located at what height above the floor
n: Vertical door pulls, centered 900 mm above the floor, are preferred to horizontal pulls on swing doors. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Doors.

q: Minimum clear width of bedroom door
n: BP 220 sets door clear widths of 0.80 m (main), 0.70 m (service and bedroom) and 0.60 m (bathroom). Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Doors and Windows.

q: Under Batas Pambansa Blg. 220, which governs design standards for economic and socialized housing projects, what is the minimum required height for a main entrance door?
n: BP 220 requires a door clear height of 2.00 m. Bathroom and mezzanine doors may be 1.80 m. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Doors and Windows.

q: How many cars can perpendicularly park in a 30.00 m strip?
n: A perpendicular car slot is 2.50 m wide, so 30.00 ÷ 2.50 = 12 cars. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.4.b.

q: If using parallel parking, how many cars can park on a 30.00 m strip?
n: A parallel car slot is 2.15 m × 6.00 m, so 30.00 ÷ 6.00 = 5 cars. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.4.b.

q: Occupant load for apartments
n: Table XII.1 gives apartments, hotels and dormitories 18.60 m² per occupant. Dwellings get 28.00 m². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Table XII.1.
